t.5.19.1: Having heard those words of that fierce rākṣasa, Sītā, distressed and with a pitiful voice, slowly replied in piteous words.
t.5.19.2: Sītā, the wretched one, afflicted with sorrow, weeping and trembling, the fair-hipped lady devoted to her husband, thought only of her lord.
t.5.19.3: Placing a blade of grass between them, she of pure smile replied: "Turn your mind away from me; let your mind be set upon your own people."
t.5.19.4: It is not fitting for you to solicit me, just as it is not fitting for an evildoer to seek spiritual perfection. I, a woman devoted to one husband, born in a great family and married into a virtuous house, must not do what is forbidden and condemned.
t.5.19.5: Having spoken thus to Rāvaṇa, the illustrious Vaidehī turned her back on that rākṣasa and spoke these words once more.
t.5.19.6: I am not a suitable wife for you, for I am the chaste wife of another. Consider dharma well, and practise well the vow of the virtuous.
t.5.19.7: Just as your own wives are to be protected, so are the wives of others, O night-roamer. Taking yourself as the measure, let delight be found in your own wives.
t.5.19.8: The wives of others lead to ruin the fickle man of restless senses who is not content with his own wives, and his mind bent on deceit as well.
t.5.19.10: Having come under a king who lacks self-discipline and delights in misconduct, even prosperous kingdoms and cities perish.
t.5.19.9: Either there are no good men here, or you do not follow the good, for, with your mind wrongly directed, you do not heed the wholesome words spoken by the wise.
t.5.19.11: So too this Laṅkā, teeming with heaps of jewels, having come into your hands, will before long perish because of your offense alone.
t.5.19.12: O Rāvaṇa, all beings rejoice at the destruction of a short-sighted doer of evil deeds who is being struck down by his own actions.
t.5.19.13: Thus the people you have wronged will speak of you, the doer of evil deeds, rejoicing and saying, "By good fortune this cruel one has met with this calamity!"
t.5.19.14: I cannot be tempted by sovereignty or by wealth. I am inseparable from Rāghava, as light is from the sun.
t.5.19.15: Having laid my head upon the honored arm of that lord of the world, how could I ever lay it upon the arm of any other?
t.5.19.16: I am the fitting wife of that very lord of the earth alone, just as sacred knowledge belongs to a self-realized brahmin who has completed his vows and the ritual bath.
t.5.19.17: Do what is right, Rāvaṇa: reunite me, sorrowing as I am, with Rāma, as one would unite a lord of elephants in the forest with his she-elephant in season.
t.5.19.18: If you wish to keep your position and do not desire a terrible death, you should make Rāma, that bull among men, your fitting friend.
t.5.19.20: You will hear the mighty-sounding twang of Rāma's bow, like the roar of a thunderbolt hurled by Śatakratu.
t.5.19.19: One might escape the thunderbolt once it is hurled, and Death might pass one by for a long while, but that Rāghava, lord of the world, once enraged, would not spare one such as you.
t.5.19.21: Here, swiftly, will fall the well-jointed arrows marked with the names of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, like serpents with blazing mouths.
t.5.19.22: Falling all around in this city and striking down the rākṣasas on every side, the heron-feathered arrows will leave no room for anyone to move.
t.5.19.23: That mighty Garuḍa that is Rāma will swiftly snatch up these great serpents, the lords of the Rākṣasas, just as Vainateya carries off snakes.
t.5.19.24: My husband, the subduer of foes, will swiftly take me away from you, just as Viṣṇu with his three strides took the blazing Śrī away from the Asuras.
t.5.19.25: When the army of the rākṣasas was struck down at Janasthāna, the place of their slaughter, you, powerless to face him, committed this truly ignoble deed, a deed worthy of a rākṣasa.
t.5.19.26: But it was only after entering the empty hermitage of those two lion-like men, when the brothers had gone off afield, that you carried me away, O vilest one.
t.5.19.27: For having caught the scent of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, you will not be able to stand within their sight, just as a dog cannot stand within sight of two tigers.
t.5.19.29: Swiftly will that lord of mine, Rāma, together with Saumitri, take away your life with his arrows, as the sun takes up a little water.
t.5.19.28: In your war with those two, your attempt to seize the pair will not hold; as with Vṛtra and the two arms of Indra, it will be a single arm held down by them.
t.5.19.30: Even if you go to Kubera's mountain or to his abode, or to the assembly hall of King Varuṇa, you will without doubt not escape from Dāśarathi, just as a great tree doomed by time does not escape the thunderbolt.
